B14_00: Negative regulation of complement keeps this amplifying protease cascade aimed at pathogens rather than host tissue. C1 inhibitor restrains initiation proteases, C4b-binding protein and CD46 act as factor I cofactors, CD55 accelerates convertase decay and CD59 blocks membrane attack complex formation. Deficiencies cause hereditary angioedema and complement-mediated haemolysis, and these regulators shape tolerance and inflammation in kidney, eye and blood.
B14_01: Prepulse inhibition, in which a weak stimulus dampens startle to a following loud one, measures sensorimotor gating and is impaired in schizophrenia, autism and Tourette syndrome. Dopamine D2 and D3 receptors and the dopamine transporter set striatal tone, opposed by adenosine A2A receptors, with glutamatergic receptor input; CNTNAP2, MDGA1, CHD8 and PTEN link the trait to neurodevelopmental wiring.
B14_02: Repulsive axon guidance halts or slows growth cones so they turn away, stall or prune branches. Class 3 and 5 semaphorins act via neuropilin-1 and plexin-A to collapse growth cones, Slit repels axons from the midline, and Wnt-Ryk signalling sets anteroposterior guidance. Loss causes misrouted projections and defective commissures, and these cues later restrain regeneration after injury.
B14_03: Dampening the IRE1 arm of the unfolded protein response, which acts through XBP1 splicing and stress kinases, lets cells end signalling once ER folding recovers and avoid apoptosis. BiP and ERdj4 hold IRE1 inactive, TMBIM6 and the UFM1 components UFL1 and DDRGK1 modulate it, and BFAR adds anti-apoptotic control, relevant to secretory cells, metabolic disease and neurodegeneration.
B14_04: This pathway restrains Th1 immunity, which defends against intracellular pathogens but causes tissue damage and autoimmunity if unchecked. IL-27, signalling through IL27RA and IL6ST, limits Th1 and Th17 differentiation; TIM-3 bound by galectin-9 drives effector T cell exhaustion; an IL-18 binding protein neutralises IL-18; and IL-33 via IL1RL1 shifts responses toward type 2 immunity. Excess restraint in tumours impairs antitumour immunity.
B14_05: This programme limits cytotoxic T cell killing so healthy tissue is spared, as inhibitory receptors recruit phosphatases or ITIM signalling to dampen TCR signalling. HLA-G recognised by KLRD1-KLRC1 and LILRB1 marks cells as protected, a mechanism exploited at the maternal-fetal interface and by tumours; CEACAM1, FCGR2B, CD45 and calcineurin tune signal strength. Too little restraint promotes autoimmunity and rejection, too much tumour and viral persistence.
B14_06: These brakes limit the strength and duration of TNF receptor signalling, whose persistence drives chronic inflammation, insulin resistance and tissue destruction. TAX1BP1 and TANK dampen receptor complexes, XIAP, NOL3 and CARD16 block death and inflammasome output, PTPN2 and PP2A reverse phosphorylation, and the decoy receptor TNFRSF11B sequesters ligand; adiponectin, apolipoprotein A-I, NR1H4 and microRNAs add further tuning.
B14_07: These signals restrain endothelial chemotaxis, keeping established vessels quiescent, limiting excess sprouting in wounds and resisting tumour angiogenesis; their loss yields disorganised, leaky vessels. Thrombospondin-1 and histidine-rich glycoprotein counteract pro-migratory growth factor and integrin signals, Notch1 enforces stalk-cell over tip-cell behaviour, and microRNAs suppress pro-angiogenic transcripts.
B14_08: This programme restrains naive CD4 T cell differentiation into Th2 cells producing IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13, whose unchecked expansion drives allergy, asthma and eosinophilia. BCL6 represses Th2 genes and supports follicular helper identity, HLX and ASCL2 bias fate away from Th2, SOCS5 dampens IL-4 receptor-STAT6 signalling, and ANXA1 contributes anti-inflammatory signals, keeping type 2 immunity proportionate.
B14_09: This braking programme limits endothelial responses to VEGF, maintaining vascular quiescence and orderly vessel patterning; its loss contributes to tumour vascularisation and proliferative retinopathy. Decorin, EMILIN1, histidine-rich glycoprotein and an ADAMTS protease limit growth factor access, angiopoietin-1-TIE signalling stabilises vessels, Sprouty2 and DAB2IP attenuate kinase output, and NR2F2, SEMA6A, ADGRA2, IL-12 and microRNAs such as miR-424 add control.
B14_10: These brakes limit FGF receptor signalling, keeping limb, skeletal, lung and kidney development in bounds and restraining angiogenesis and oncogenic FGFR activity. FGF-induced Sprouty proteins feed back on RAS-ERK, glypican and the sulfatases SULF1 and SULF2 alter heparan sulfate-dependent ligand-receptor binding, SHISA2 retains receptors in the ER, and OFD1, GATA3, PRDM14 and microRNAs act indirectly.
B14_11: IL-6 drives acute-phase responses, fever and Th17 and plasma cell differentiation, and unchecked signalling sustains rheumatoid arthritis, cytokine storm and inflammation-associated cancer. This braking layer acts on the receptor-JAK-STAT3 axis: PTPN2 dephosphorylates JAKs and STAT3, gp130 activity is limited, and microRNAs including let-7, miR-125 and miR-146 repress IL-6 and pathway transcripts, resolving inflammation.
B14_12: Negative regulation of monocyte chemotaxis limits monocyte influx to injured or infected tissue, shaping prolonged inflammation, atherosclerosis, fibrosis and wound healing. Secreted CCN3, NBL1 and GREM1 act in the extracellular milieu, SLIT2 via Robo blocks myeloid migration, DUSP1 shortens MAP kinase signalling, and SLAMF8 tempers macrophage responses, together braking innate immune cell trafficking.
B14_13: These brakes lower cytokine production by activated T cells, limiting tissue damage, enforcing tolerance and, in tumours, blunting immunity; loss causes autoimmunity, as FOXP3 mutations show. BTLA engaging HVEM and LILRB4 deliver inhibitory signals, arginase depletes arginine, SMAD7 acts in TGF-beta signalling, type I interferons can suppress, and TBX21 shapes which cytokines helper cells produce.
B14_14: This pathway dampens VEGF receptor signalling in endothelial cells, limiting sprouting, permeability and proliferation; loss contributes to abnormal angiogenesis in tumours, retinopathy and vascular malformations. Mechanisms include receptor internalisation and degradation via NEDD4, HGS and epsins, dephosphorylation by PTPN1, Ras restraint by DAB2IP, the matrix and junction proteins EMILIN1, MMRN2 and CADM4, and transcriptional and microRNA control.
B14_15: These processes brake granulocyte chemotaxis so neutrophil and eosinophil influx resolves rather than damaging tissue; loss favours persistent inflammation in sepsis, arthritis and chronic lung disease. A decoy-like anaphylatoxin receptor tempers C5a receptor signalling, a cell-surface peptidase trims chemokines, an axon guidance cue repels leukocytes, a hyaluronan-binding protein limits transmigration, and a myeloid microRNA restrains granulocyte activation.
B14_16: Dampening the PERK arm of the unfolded protein response lets cells restore protein synthesis and avoid apoptosis once ER stress resolves. GADD34 and CReP direct eIF2α dephosphorylation to close the feedback loop, BiP holds PERK inactive, PTPN1 acts on the kinase, NCK adaptors and AKT couple growth signalling to attenuation, and DDRGK1 links the pathway to ufmylation-based ER quality control.
B14_17: These brakes dampen cellular responses to TGF-beta, which drives growth arrest, matrix production and epithelial-mesenchymal transition, to prevent fibrosis, scarring and tumour promotion. MicroRNAs, several TGF-beta induced as feedback, target receptors, SMADs and effectors; PPARG antagonises fibrogenic programmes and IL4 reflects immune cross-talk. Loss contributes to organ fibrosis, while excess removes the cytostatic protection TGF-beta provides.
B14_18: This pathway sets how much ER stress cells tolerate before mitochondrial apoptosis, crucial for secretory cells such as beta cells, plasma cells and osteoblasts; WFS1 mutation in Wolfram syndrome causes diabetes. Mechanisms include XBP1 and CREB3 transcription, chaperone induction, ER-associated degradation via SYVN1 and HERPUD1, TMBIM calcium buffering and BCL2L1 suppression of permeabilisation, with PRKN, PARK7 and OPA1 linking it to neuronal survival.
B14_19: This restraint keeps vascular smooth muscle cells from migrating toward chemoattractants, opposing neointimal thickening after angioplasty, transplant vasculopathy and atherosclerotic plaque formation. A Slit ligand repels cells via Robo receptors, a coronin constrains lamellipodial protrusion, a glutathione transferase limits pro-motility redox signalling, and a microRNA suppresses pro-migratory transcripts, opposing growth factor-driven chemotaxis.
B14_20: Negative regulation of BMP signalling controls skeletal patterning, joint and vascular development and iron homeostasis. Noggin, chordin, gremlins, twisted gastrulation and sclerostin sequester ligands, a pseudoreceptor and BMPER tune receptor access, SMAD6 and SMAD7 with SMURF ligases degrade components, and phosphatases, SKI/SKIL, TOB1 and microRNAs silence output. Loss causes heterotopic ossification and sclerosing bone disease, and TMPRSS6 links it to iron loading.
B14_21: This braking programme keeps antibody-triggered complement destruction aimed at pathogens; failure underlies atypical haemolytic uraemic syndrome, macular degeneration and lupus-like autoimmunity. C4b-binding protein, CD46 and complement receptor 1 dismantle the C3 and C5 convertases and act as factor I cofactors, while the inhibitory Fc receptor FCGR2B recruits SHP-1 via an ITIM to raise B cell and myeloid activation thresholds.
B14_22: Dampening chemokine signalling determines when leukocytes stop following gradients, limiting inflammatory infiltration. SLIT ligands acting through ROBO1 blunt chemotaxis of leukocytes, neurons and tumour cells, SH2B3 restrains kinase signalling, small RNAs lower chemokine and receptor transcripts, and PADI2 citrullination weakens chemokines. Loss favours persistent recruitment, and SLIT-ROBO links this biology to axon guidance and vascular patterning.
B14_23: This programme restrains naive CD4 T cell commitment to the Th17 lineage, whose IL-17-producing cells drive neutrophilic inflammation in psoriasis, inflammatory bowel disease and other autoimmunity. TBX21 suppresses the Th17 programme, STAT5A downstream of IL-2 and JAK3 competes with STAT3, and CD69 and galectin-1 tune responses to polarising cues, placing the pathway within differentiation and peripheral tolerance.
B14_24: Negative regulation of macrophage chemotaxis slows or stops macrophage migration to sites of injury or infection, preventing persistent infiltrates and collateral damage. Contributors include cytokine-like mediators, a complement component whose cleavage products are chemoattractants, a matrix metalloproteinase, a signalling adaptor and a SLAM-family receptor, while an estrogen-synthesising enzyme links sex hormones to inflammation and wound healing.
B14_25: This pathway limits ER-associated degradation, giving slow-folding or regulated ER proteins a chance to fold or act rather than being retrotranslocated and destroyed by the proteasome. A small VCP-interacting protein and UBX cofactors compete for the p97 motor, SGTA holds extracted substrates, and USP14 and USP25 trim ubiquitin to rescue clients; AQP11 links this control to renal proximal tubule integrity.
